source.text: Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς καὶ Τιμόθεος τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ καὶ κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη.

records.literal_gloss: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of [the] Thessalonians in God Father and Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace.

en.L: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}: grace to you and peace.
en.B: From Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians, which belongs to God the Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Grace and peace to you.
en.R: This letter is from Paul, Silvanus and Timothy. We are writing to the church in the city of Thessalonica. You belong to God the Father and to the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. May God show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.choice: Silvanus: the Silas of Acts
decisions.reason: Σιλουανὸς is the Latin form of the name Silas. He traveled with Paul on the journey that brought the gospel to Philippi and Thessalonica (Acts 15:40; 16:19-40; 17:1-10). Timothy was with them (Acts 16:1-3; 17:14).

decisions.choice: the Thessalonians: the church in Thessalonica, the chief city of Macedonia
decisions.reason: Thessalonica was the capital of the Roman province of Macedonia, a port on the main road across northern Greece. Paul founded the church there after leaving Philippi and had to leave soon because of opposition (Acts 17:1-10). This letter is usually thought to be one of the earliest of Paul's letters.

decisions.choice: in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: the church lives in union with God and Christ
decisions.reason: ἐν ("in") describes the church itself: it belongs to God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ and lives in them. Paul names God and Jesus together under one preposition.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "grace to you and peace"
alternatives: adds "from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ", the wording of Paul's other greetings. Important early manuscripts have the short greeting, and a copyist is more likely to have added the familiar words than to have dropped them.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: which belongs to
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "in God" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: May God show you grace and give you peace
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as in Philippians 1:2 and Colossians 1:2.

source.text: Εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν μνείαν ποιούμενοι ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν ἡμῶν, ἀδιαλείπτως μνημονεύοντες ὑμῶν τοῦ ἔργου τῆς πίστεως καὶ τοῦ κόπου τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ τῆς ὑπομονῆς τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν, εἰδότες, ἀδελφοὶ ἠγαπημένοι ὑπὸ θεοῦ, τὴν ἐκλογὴν ὑμῶν, ὅτι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐγενήθη εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐν λόγῳ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν δυνάμει καὶ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πληροφορίᾳ πολλῇ, καθὼς οἴδατε οἷοι ἐγενήθημεν ἐν ὑμῖν δι’ ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: We give thanks to the God always concerning all of you, mention making in the prayers of us, \v 3 unceasingly remembering of you the work of the faith and the labor of the love and the endurance of the hope of the Lord of us Jesus Christ before the God and Father of us, \v 4 knowing, brothers having been loved by God, the election of you, \v 5 because the gospel of us not came to you in word only but also in power and in [the] Holy Spirit and [in] much full assurance, just as you know what kind [of men] we were among you for your sake;

en.L: We give thanks to God always for all of you, making mention [of you] in our prayers, \v 3 unceasingly remembering your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} before our God and Father, \v 4 knowing, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} loved by God, your election, \v 5 because our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power and in [the] Holy Spirit and with much full assurance, just as you know what kind [of men] we were among you for your sake.
en.B: Every time we mention you in our prayers, we give thanks to God for all of you. \v 3 Before our God and Father we never stop remembering the work your faith does, the labor your love takes on, and the endurance your hope in our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives you. \v 4 {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}} loved by God, we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen you, \v 5 because our gospel came to you not only in words but also with power, with the Holy Spirit and with full certainty. You know what kind of people we were among you for your sake.
en.R: We always thank God for all of you, and we pray for you all the time. \v 3 When we talk to God our Father, we always remember what your faith leads you to do, how hard you work because you love others, and how you keep going because you hope in our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 4 {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, God loves you, and we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \v 5 We know this because when we brought you the good news, it did not come with words only. It came with power and with the Holy Spirit, and we were completely sure it was true. You know how we lived among you to help you.

decisions.choice: "always" goes with the thanks; "unceasingly" goes with the remembering
decisions.reason: πάντοτε ("always") stands with "we give thanks", as in Colossians 1:3. The SBLGNT puts a comma before ἀδιαλείπτως ("unceasingly"), so it begins the next phrase: they keep remembering what the Thessalonians do.

decisions.choice: faith, love and hope, each shown in action: work that faith produces, labor that love takes on, endurance that hope gives
decisions.reason: Each genitive names the source: faith works, love toils, hope endures. Paul joins the same three again in 5:8 and in 1 Corinthians 13:13 and Colossians 1:4-5. κόπου is hard, wearying labor.

decisions.choice: hope in our Lord Jesus Christ: hope fixed on him, above all on his coming
alternatives: "of our Lord Jesus Christ" goes with all three: faith, love and hope
decisions.reason: τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ most naturally goes with ἐλπίδος: the hope that looks to Jesus, who is coming from heaven (verse 10).

decisions.choice: before our God and Father: in their prayers, in God's presence
alternatives: their endurance as people who will stand before God
decisions.reason: The phrase may say where Paul remembers them, in prayer before God, or look ahead to the day they will stand before him (2:19; 3:13). The first fits the opening "we give thanks" and "in our prayers".

decisions.choice: election: God's choosing them to be his people
decisions.reason: ἐκλογὴν is God's choice of a people for himself, as he chose Israel (Deuteronomy 7:6-8). Gentile believers in Thessalonica are now "loved by God" and chosen (Colossians 3:12).

decisions.choice: because: the reason Paul knows they are chosen
decisions.reason: ὅτι gives the evidence: the way the gospel came to them, with power and the Spirit, and the way they received it (verse 6).

decisions.choice: full assurance: the deep conviction with which the gospel was preached
alternatives: the conviction the gospel produced in the hearers
decisions.reason: πληροφορίᾳ means full certainty. Since the sentence is about how the gospel came, the conviction is most likely the preachers', though the Spirit's power worked in the hearers too.

decisions.choice: our gospel: the gospel we preached
decisions.reason: Not a different gospel, but the message Paul and his companions brought (2:2 calls it "the gospel of God").

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: what kind [of men] we were (L); what kind of people we were (B); how we lived among you (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "what sort"; the word is masculine and refers to Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, so Literal brackets "men".

decisions.choice: what your faith leads you to do, how hard you work because you love others, and how you keep going because you hope
alternatives: your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the three genitives (m2).

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς μιμηταὶ ἡμῶν ἐγενήθητε καὶ τοῦ κυρίου, δεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον ἐν θλίψει πολλῇ μετὰ χαρᾶς πνεύματος ἁγίου, ὥστε γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς τύπον πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐν τῇ Μακεδονίᾳ καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἀχαΐᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: And you imitators of us became and of the Lord, having received the word in tribulation much with joy of [the] Holy Spirit, \v 7 so that you became an example to all the believing [ones] in the Macedonia and in the Achaia.

en.L: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with [the] joy of [the] Holy Spirit, \v 7 so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
en.B: You became imitators of us and of the Lord. Though the word brought you great affliction, you received it with joy that came from the Holy Spirit, \v 7 so that you set an example for every believer in Macedonia and Achaia.
en.R: You began to live the way we live and the way the Lord lived. You suffered a lot when you accepted God's message, but the Holy Spirit gave you joy. \v 7 So you became an example for all the believers in the regions of Macedonia and Achaia.

decisions.choice: imitators: people who follow another's example
decisions.reason: μιμηταὶ means one who imitates. They followed the example of Paul and his companions, and of the Lord Jesus himself, who also suffered (1 Corinthians 11:1; 2:14-15).

decisions.choice: much affliction: the opposition the church met from the start
decisions.reason: Acts 17:5-9 tells how a mob attacked the house where Paul stayed and dragged believers before the city officials. The trouble went on after Paul left (2:14; 3:3-4).

decisions.choice: joy of the Holy Spirit: joy the Spirit gives
decisions.reason: The joy comes from the Spirit (Galatians 5:22), and it came in the middle of suffering.

decisions.choice: Macedonia and Achaia: the two Roman provinces of Greece
decisions.reason: Macedonia in the north included Philippi and Thessalonica; Achaia in the south included Athens and Corinth, where Paul was when he wrote (Acts 18:1-5).

decisions.choice: example: a pattern for others to follow
decisions.reason: τύπον is a model or pattern (Philippians 3:17). A young church became a pattern for older ones.

decisions.choice: Though the word brought you great affliction, you received it with joy
alternatives: having received the word in much affliction with joy
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the contrast between affliction and joy explicit.

decisions.choice: the way the Lord lived; the regions of
alternatives: imitators of the Lord; in Macedonia and Achaia
decisions.reason: Readable says what imitating the Lord means here and that Macedonia and Achaia are regions.

source.text: ἀφ’ ὑμῶν γὰρ ἐξήχηται ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου οὐ μόνον ἐν τῇ Μακεδονίᾳ καὶ Ἀχαΐᾳ, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἐξελήλυθεν, ὥστε μὴ χρείαν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς λαλεῖν τι·

records.literal_gloss: From you for has sounded forth the word of the Lord not only in the Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place the faith of you, the [faith] toward the God, has gone out, so that no need to have us to say anything;

en.L: For from you the word of the Lord has sounded forth not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need to say anything.
en.B: The word of the Lord has echoed out from you, and not only through Macedonia and Achaia: in every place people have heard of your faith in God. So there is nothing we need to say.
en.R: People in Macedonia and Achaia have heard the Lord's message from you. And not only there: people everywhere have heard that you have faith in God. So we do not need to tell anyone about it.

decisions.choice: has sounded forth: rung out, like a trumpet or an echo
decisions.reason: ἐξήχηται is found only here in the New Testament. It is used of a sound that rings out and carries. The perfect says it is still sounding.

decisions.choice: the sentence changes course
decisions.reason: Paul begins "not only in Macedonia and Achaia", then, instead of finishing "but everywhere", starts again with a new subject: "in every place your faith has gone out".

decisions.choice: in every place: far and wide
decisions.reason: A way of saying the news has spread widely, as in Romans 1:8. Thessalonica lay on a main road and was a busy port, so news traveled from it quickly.

decisions.choice: we do not need to tell anyone about it
alternatives: we have no need to say anything
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul does not need to say.

source.text: αὐτοὶ γὰρ περὶ ἡμῶν ἀπαγγέλλουσιν ὁποίαν εἴσοδον ἔσχομεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ πῶς ἐπεστρέψατε πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἀπὸ τῶν εἰδώλων δουλεύειν θεῷ ζῶντι καὶ ἀληθινῷ, καὶ ἀναμένειν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν, ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦν τὸν ῥυόμενον ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ὀργῆς τῆς ἐρχομένης.

records.literal_gloss: they themselves for concerning us report what kind of entrance we had to you, and how you turned to the God from the idols to serve [as slaves] a God living and true, \v 10 and to wait for the Son of him from the heavens, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus, the [one] rescuing us from the wrath the coming.

en.L: For they themselves report about us what kind of welcome we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve as slaves a living and true God, \v 10 and to wait for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son from the heavens, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised from the dead, Jesus, who rescues us from the coming wrath.
en.B: Everywhere people tell of the welcome you gave us, and how you turned to God from idols, to be slaves of the living and true God \v 10 and to wait for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son from heaven. God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead: Jesus, who rescues us from the wrath that is coming.
en.R: Everywhere people talk about how you welcomed us. They tell how you turned away from idols to God, to be slaves who serve the God who is alive and true. \v 10 They tell how you are waiting for God's Son to come back from heaven. This is Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He is the one who rescues us from God's anger, which is coming.

decisions.choice: welcome: the kind of reception they gave
alternatives: entrance: how Paul came among them
decisions.reason: εἴσοδον means an entrance or a visit, and so the reception a visitor is given. 2:1 uses the same word for Paul's visit.

decisions.choice: turned to God from idols: most of the church had been pagans
decisions.reason: Acts 17:4 says some Jews believed, with many Greeks who worshiped God; but these words show that most of the church had worshiped the gods of the city.

decisions.choice: serve as slaves: belong wholly to God
decisions.reason: δουλεύω is to serve as a slave. Those who served idols now belong to the living God (Romans 6:22).

decisions.choice: a living and true God: unlike lifeless idols
decisions.reason: The prophets set the living God against idols that cannot see or act (Jeremiah 10:10).

decisions.choice: wait for his Son from heaven: wait for his return
decisions.reason: They are waiting for Jesus to come from heaven, as 4:16 describes. Waiting was part of their new life from the start.

decisions.choice: who rescues us: Jesus' work as rescuer, at the coming judgment
decisions.reason: The present participle ῥυόμενον works almost like a title: Jesus is the one who rescues. The rescue is from τῆς ὀργῆς τῆς ἐρχομένης, God's judgment at the end (5:9).

decisions.choice: serve as slaves (L); be slaves of (B); be slaves who serve (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to serve as a slave, and the style guide keeps "slave" at every level (m3).

decisions.choice: Everywhere people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are: people in the places of verse 8.

decisions.choice: God's anger, which is coming
decisions.reason: Plainer words for "wrath" (m6).
